Under Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions (BCs), the large coefficient matrices are banded, enabling efficient diagonalization of the small $r \times r$ factor matrix and reducing the per-step computational complexity to $O((m+n)r^2)$ and storage to $O((m+n)r)$. For periodic BCs, we combine this diagonalization strategy with a rank-2 Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury update to handle wrap-around corner entries at negligible additional cost. Numerical experiments demonstrate first-order temporal and $(k+1)$th-order spatial convergence of the proposed BUG-MLFEM in the discrete $L^2$ norm, where $k$ denotes the polynomial degree of the finite element space, together with significant computational speedups over existing low-rank integrators.

title: Some remarks on nonexistence in the Gamow liquid drop model
summary: In this paper we deal with the celebrated Gamow liquid drop model, namely, for $m>0$, $N\geq 2$ and $α\in (0,N)$, we study the problem \[ \min\Big\{P(Ω)+ V_α(Ω) : Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^N,\;|Ω|=m\Big\}\,, \] and focus mostly on the nonexistence of minimizers for large masses. First we show that any possible minimizer in the asymptotic regime must satisfy an optimal thickness property. Eventually, in the simplified setting of sets made up as a tiling of cubes, we show that nonexistence occurs for large masses for the whole range of parameters $N\geq 2$ and $α\in (0,N)$.

title: Two-level additive Schwarz preconditioners with GDSW coarse spaces for high-order discretizations in 2D
summary: Two-level overlapping Schwarz preconditioners with Generalized Dryja-Smith-Widlund (GDSW) and Reduced GDSW (RGDSW) coarse spaces for high-order finite element methods (FEM) and virtual element methods (VEM) are investigated and applied to the Poisson problem in 2D. The GDSW coarse space is a well-established robust choice for preconditioners in domain decomposition, while the RGDSW coarse space offers a competitive alternative by reducing the coarse problem dimension while maintaining robustness. On the theoretical side, a condition number bound for both preconditioners is proved for conforming $\mathbb{P}_k$ and $\mathbb{Q}_k$ finite element spaces with explicit dependence on the polynomial degree $k$. Through numerical experiments on structured triangular and quadrilateral meshes for FEM and on polygonal meshes for VEM, it is demonstrated that both GDSW and RGDSW maintain scalability properties across polynomial orders up to $k=9$ for selected degrees. The RGDSW approach achieves a reduction in the coarse problem dimension by a factor of approximately three compared to GDSW while maintaining competitive iteration counts.

title: One-dimensional pressureless flow with a nonlinear velocity law: Bregman variational construction and well-posedness
summary: We establish global existence, uniqueness and quantitative stability for one-dimensional pressureless flow governed by \[ \partial_tρ+\partial_x\bigl(ρf(u)\bigr)=0, \qquad \partial_t(ρu)+\partial_x\bigl(ρu f(u)\bigr)=0, \] where $ρ$ is the mass density, possibly measure-valued, $u$ is the physical velocity, and $f\in C^1(\mathbb R)$, with $f'>0$, determines the transport velocity $f(u)$. The initial mass has finite positive mass and finite second moment, allowing atoms and unbounded support, and the initial physical velocity is bounded. The difficulty at a cluster collision is that mass and momentum conservation determine a mass-weighted average of physical velocity, whereas transport is governed by the nonlinear law $f$ applied to that average. We construct global entropy solutions by a Bregman variational time discretization whose cost is chosen to reproduce the transport velocity determined by this mass-weighted average, coupled with conditional-expectation updates of physical velocity. For every entropy solution satisfying the Oleinik condition on the transport velocity and initial weak continuity of the kinetic energy measure, we establish a Lagrangian representation and prove uniqueness within this class by comparing flows with possibly different cluster intervals. For two such solutions with the same velocity law and common mass, we obtain a $W_\infty$ estimate for the normalized mass measures in terms of the initial position and physical-velocity discrepancies in mass coordinates, whenever the initial $W_\infty$ distance is finite. The Lagrangian evolution has the semigroup property.

title: A two-level preconditioner for discontinuous virtual element methods with irregular subdomains
summary: We introduce and analyze a two-level overlapping additive Schwarz preconditioner for discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of virtual element spaces on general polygonal meshes in two dimensions, for a second-order elliptic problem whose coefficient is constant on each subdomain and may have large jumps across the interface. The discretization is a weighted symmetric interior penalty formulation: the averages carry the coefficient and the penalty is scaled by its harmonic mean across each edge, which keeps the method consistent and makes the constants of the analysis independent of the coefficient. The coarse space is obtained from a virtual, continuous partition of unity with a single degree of freedom per subdomain vertex, and is therefore applicable to the irregular subdomains produced by a graph partitioner; the discrete harmonic extension used to build it may be replaced by a cheaper projection onto polynomials of low degree. We prove that the condition number of the preconditioned system is bounded by $C(1+\log(H/h))(1+H/δ)$, where $H$, $h$ and $δ$ denote the subdomain diameter, the mesh size and the overlap, and where $C$ is independent of the number of subdomains and of the contrast of the coefficient, provided the latter is quasi-monotone. This is the same bound known for the conforming case and the analysis allows for hanging nodes. We also show, by an explicit example, that the quasi-monotonicity assumption cannot be dispensed with. Numerical experiments with structured triangular, hexagonal and Voronoi meshes, and with subdomains obtained both by uniform partitioning and by METIS, confirm the theory.

title: Spectral stability of resonant Y-solitons for the KP-II equation
summary: The KP-II equation was introduced by Kadomtsev and Petviashvili to explain the transverse stability of line solitary waves in shallow water. Using Darboux transformations, we prove the spectral stability of Y-shaped line solitons in an exponentially weighted space that captures the amount of waves receding behind the line solitons. We show that the spectrum of the linearized operator consists of the continuous spectrum of the zero background together with three residual spectral domains whose boundaries contain continuous spectra associated with the constituent line solitons. Exploiting the analytic dependence of the pairings with adjoint eigenfunctions on the spectral parameters, we prove that the orthogonality conditions associated with all adjoint eigenfunctions can be reduced to orthogonality conditions against three families of adjoint continuous eigenfunctions. Moreover, we investigate linear stability of Y-solitons in a subspace satisfying orthogonality conditions against adjoint continuous eigenfunctions associated with outgoing modulations along each line soliton constituting the Y-soliton.

title: Fully discrete multi-entropy-stable compact Runge--Kutta discontinuous Galerkin methods for hyperbolic conservation laws
summary: We develop fully discrete multi-entropy-stable high-order compact Runge--Kutta discontinuous Galerkin (cRKDG) methods for hyperbolic conservation laws. Our main result is a weak cell entropy inequality for multi-dimensional systems after one full high-order Runge--Kutta (RK) time step. The proof exploits the cell-local intermediate stages of cRKDG: their perturbations are controlled by the initial in-cell variation. The analysis does not require a strong stability preserving decomposition or stagewise entropy correction. For a sufficiently dissipative Lax--Friedrichs flux and explicit RK methods with nonnegative output weights, the inequality holds under a suitable time-step restriction for strongly convex entropy pairs. For a prescribed, uniformly conditioned family of such entropies, common dissipation and time-step conditions ensure weak cell entropy stability for all entropy pairs. A single cell-average-preserving scaling at the end of each step then enforces all corresponding strong cell entropy inequalities simultaneously. We also prove a Lax--Wendroff-type theorem: under the stated assumptions, any strongly convergent sequence of numerical solutions converges to a weak solution satisfying all prescribed entropy inequalities. Numerical experiments in one and two dimensions demonstrate high-order accuracy, the benefit of multiple entropy constraints for nonconvex scalar problems, and robust performance on shock problems.

title: Boundedness and exponential stabilization in a degenerate migration-consumption system with logistic damping
summary: We study the no-flux problem for a taxis-type migration-consumption system with logistic damping in a bounded planar domain, where the motility function \(φ\) vanishes at zero and degenerates algebraically of order \(α\ge1\). We prove uniform boundedness in \(L^\infty(Ω)\times W^{1,\infty}(Ω)\) for every fixed damping coefficient \(b>0\), without any smallness assumption on the initial data, thus improving the previous \(L^2\)-boundedness results. For \(α>1\), we further prove that the solution converges exponentially to the spatially homogeneous state \((a/b,0)\), with an explicit admissible rate. The proof combines a weighted Gagliardo--Nirenberg type inequality adapted to the degeneracy with the dissipative structure of the signal equation. Therefore logistic damping drives the system toward homogeneity, despite the loss of uniform elliptic regularization.

title: Global Regularization of the Spatial Elliptic Restricted Three-body Problem: Quaternionic, Hamiltonian Formulation
summary: Any objects in space may encounter singularity due to the inverse-square law of the gravitational force, hindering the analysis and propagation of particle motion in space. Regularization in celestial mechanics removes such gravitational singularities in equations of motion by transforming the time and coordinates. This paper addresses a class of regularization methods known as global regularization for restricted three-body problems (R3BPs), which simultaneously removes the two singularities (e.g., Earth and Moon in cislunar space). It enables analysis, propagation, and prediction of particle motion throughout the domain of R3BPs, which is in stark contrast to regularizing each singularity individually. In particular, this paper develops a formulation for global regularization of the spatial elliptic R3BP (ER3BP) under external perturbations. The presented formulation leverages mathematical tools from quaternionic (hyper-complex) algebra and Hamiltonian mechanics. This approach enables us to (i) elegantly handle the four-dimensional coordinates arising from the dimension-lifting operation for spatial regularization, (ii) systematically derive the coordinate-momentum transformation while preserving the canonical structure and incorporating perturbing forces, and (iii) provide geometric insights for analyzing the regularity of the transformation, resulting Hamiltonian, and dynamical flow. Numerical examples demonstrate the validity of the mathematical results as well as significant numerical benefits of the regularization formulation in perturbed Earth-Moon ER3BP.

title: The Inviscid Limit of Viscous Burgers through Shock Formation and Development
summary: We study the inviscid limit of the one-dimensional viscous Burgers equation from smooth initial data through nondegenerate shock formation and subsequent shock development. Chaturvedi and Graham \cite{CG} obtained sharp estimates of order $ν^{1/4}$ up to the shock-formation time. We extend their analysis beyond this time, comparing the viscous solution with the inviscid entropy solution evolving from the same initial data. With the shock-formation time normalized to $t=0$, we prove a pointwise error bound on a fixed interval $0\leq t \leq \bar{\varepsilon}$, where $\bar{\varepsilon}>0$ is independent of the viscosity $ν$. The bound consists of a term of order $ν^{1/4}$ and an exponentially localized contribution originating from the viscous shock layer. The proof is based on matching an outer expansion, an inner expansion near the formation point, and a viscous shock-profile expansion. Combined with the results of Chaturvedi and Graham, this yields a quantitative description of the inviscid limit from the initial time through the development of the young shock.

title: Generalized PINN-Based Inverse Estimation of Spatially Varying Heat Transfer Coefficients with Transfer Learning
summary: This study investigates generalized boundary representations and transfer learning for physics-informed neural-network (PINN) estimation of spatially varying convective heat transfer coefficients (HTCs) in jet impingement cooling. Piecewise-linear (PWL) and neural-network boundary estimators are inferred from transient interior-temperature measurements and evaluated against CFD-CHT reference HTC profiles at Reynolds numbers of 5000, 10000 and 15000. A discrete Adjoint-FEM formulation with gradient regularization based on the $H^1$-seminorm provides an independent inverse-method comparison. Transfer learning is investigated under two source-target conditions: transfer between noise levels at the same Reynolds number, and transfer from a controlled Gaussian-profile problem to CFD-CHT-derived target problems at different Reynolds numbers. For the representative Re = 5000 target with 5% measurement noise, quadratic, PWL, and neural-network PINNs achieve relative HTC-profile errors of 5.08, 5.31 and 5.19%, respectively, while generalized representations reduce the error for the Re = 15000 target from 16.76% for the quadratic PINN to 14.41% and 14.46%. Transfer learning reduces target-training time by 57.86-81.71% for fixed-Reynolds-number transfer and by 50.59-84.94% for Gaussian-to-CHT transfer. Its effect on reconstruction accuracy is target dependent: fixed-profile PWL transfer remains within 0.30 percentage points of scratch training, whereas Gaussian-to-CHT transfer produces differences of 0.10-1.52 percentage points across targets and representations. These results demonstrate that generalized PINN representations can accommodate spatially varying HTC profiles without a prescribed quadratic form, while transfer learning can substantially reduce target-training cost for repeated inverse estimation, with the resulting reconstruction accuracy depending on source-target compatibility.

title: Radial pressureless Euler flow: structure and stability of absorption at the origin
summary:
We study absorption at the origin in radial pressureless Euler flow in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq2$. For rotation-invariant nonnegative locally finite initial mass and bounded radial initial velocity vanishing at the origin, we prove global existence and uniqueness in a full-space radial entropy class with a one-sided Lipschitz bound and an initial kinetic-energy trace. Absorption is permanent, including retention of any initial origin atom.
  For finite positive mass with finite second moment, a Lagrangian projection representation characterizes the absorbed mass and its left limits at positive times through extreme minimizers of a free-position primitive. We derive a radial scalar momentum balance with a nonnegative Stieltjes boundary impulse measure. The minimum value of the same primitive yields a weighted Stieltjes identity equating accumulated time-weighted impulse with the integral of initial radii over absorbed labels, valid also for jumps and singular continuous absorption; the boundary impulse measure and the absorption measure are mutually absolutely continuous on $(0,\infty)$.
  For such finite-mass data with common total mass, strong $L^2$ convergence of initial quantiles and Lagrangian velocities, together with convergence of initial origin masses, yields convergence of absorbed mass at continuity times of the limiting absorption and local weak convergence of absorption measures on $(0,\infty)$. Finally, even with a fixed smooth initial radial probability density, every probability measure compactly supported in $(0,\infty)$ can be realized as the absorption measure by choosing a bounded radial initial velocity; in particular, purely singular continuous absorption occurs.

title: A Unified Framework for Randomized Row-Action Methods for Structured Data Fitting and Constraint Geometry
summary: We study randomized row-action methods for problems with linear observations, convex constraints, and non-Euclidean geometry. Our starting point is a unified formulation in which the data-fitting term acts in observation space, while the feasible set and the regularizer encode structure in variable space. It covers constrained least squares, nonnegative and simplex-constrained models, regularized data fitting, and equality-constrained Bregman selection problems. The structure of these problems leads naturally to two algorithmic branches. The first uses primal Bregman-proximal row steps for soft data-fitting problems. The second uses dual Bregman--Kaczmarz steps for problems with hard equality constraints. We first derive a common one-step inequality. We then give deterministic and stochastic convergence results for the soft branch under relative smoothness. For constrained least squares, the normalized row oracle has exact first- and second-moment identities. They yield an expected ergodic bound in the inconsistent case, an $O(1/K)$ bound in the interpolating case, and linear convergence of the actual iterates under a residual error bound. For equality-constrained selectors, we prove linear convergence in expected Bregman distance under a residual-to-Bregman error bound. We recall global sufficient conditions for this bound and derive local constants for the nonnegative quadratic geometry and the entropy geometry on the simplex. Numerical experiments illustrate the noisy stepsize trade-off and the local entropy selector theory, and show that entropic row-action updates can recover interpretable factors in a simplex-structured nonnegative matrix factorization problem.

title: A geometric lower bound for the clamped plate eigenvalue problem in low dimensions and extensions
summary: We show that the spectrum of the Dirichlet-biLaplacian can be quantitatively bounded from below in terms of the inradius only, for a general open set in dimensions $2$ and $3$. For the same dimensions, we also extend this result to fractional powers $s$ of the Laplacian, with $N/2<s<2$. The resulting estimate comes with a constant having the correct asymptotic behavior as $s$ approaches the two endpoints $N/2$ and $2$. The proofs exploit capacitary techniques in the vein of Maz'ya.

title: A quantum algorithm for meshless lattice Boltzmann method with unitary interpolation
summary: We present a mass-weighted meshless formulation for the shifted incompressible lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) whose streaming step is exactly unitary, combining with the Carleman embedding. In traditional meshless LBM, on a scattered node set the semi-Lagrangian streaming step is an interpolation, which is not unitary; a generic block encoding of this matrix therefore requires a normalization proportional to its sparsity and logarithmically many ancillas. To overcome the non-unitarity, we instead express the interpolation as the exponential exp(a Dx + b Dy) of mimetic derivative operators. Endowing each node with its Voronoi mass and applying a mass-weighted similarity transform renders these derivative operators skew-Hermitian by enforcing moment constraints together with low-wave number trigonometric differentiation conditions, so that the interpolation becomes exactly unitary. Such unitarization of interpolation leave the local collision step unchanged up to a rescaling of its quadratic term, where the same weights define the amplitude encoding of the distribution functions. For quasi-uniform node sets, the mass-weighting diagonal remains within a unit-order normalization that degrades only mildly as the Carleman truncation order grows, thereby mitigating the cost of block encoding. Numerical experiments on the Taylor Green vortex confirm that the method reproduces the full meshless LBM, with the velocity error decreasing as the Carleman order increases.

title: Asymptotic stability and sharp decay near homogeneous solutions of a nonlinearly damped Schrödinger equation on the torus
summary: We study the one-dimensional periodic nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a power-type nonlinear damping, both in the focusing and the defocusing regime. For a sufficiently small damping parameter and initial data close in relative $H^1$ norm to a nonzero spatially homogeneous state, we prove global existence and asymptotic convergence, after a constant phase adjustment, to an explicit homogeneous solution. The \(L^2\) and \(H^1\) norms follow the explicit adiabatic decay law, with the same leading coefficient as the homogeneous solution. We obtain explicit convergence rates, including a \(t^{-1/2}\) bound for the relative spatial perturbation. For every nonconstant initial datum in a small neighborhood of the homogeneous solution, the kinetic energy has a strictly positive leading coefficient and decays one power of time faster than the squared \(L^2\) norm.

title: Multilevel Monte Carlo for Zeroth-Order Stochastic Bilevel Optimization with Inexact Lower Level Solves
summary: Variational regularization techniques are dominant in the field of mathematical imaging. The expressiveness of these methods heavily depends on the adopted regularization formulation which usually involves a number of parameters which have to be fine-tuned by the user. To circumvent the heavy computational costs associated with this parameter tuning, data-driven learning strategies have turned out to be a useful strategy. Selecting parameters by learning from data gives rise to a hierarchical (bilevel) optimization problem, which is in general computationally hard to solve. Our aim in this paper is to develop a data-efficient solution strategy for the bilevel learning problem. To that end, we propose a multilevel Monte Carlo derivative-free optimization method that couples Gaussian smoothing of the upper-level objective (parameter selection) with a hierarchy of lower-level (variational regularization) solution accuracies. Being agnostic towards the specific way the lower-level problem is solved, we derive explicit oracle complexity and computational cost statements for approximately solving the entire bilevel learning problem. Our statements are parameterized by the employed lower-level solution method, thus allowing for a direct cost accounting from the variational reconstruction method to the parameter selection problem. This enables us to give a universal end-to-end complexity analysis of bilevel learning, valid for the most important optimization routines in inverse problems, rather than for a specific choice of methods.

title: Minimal time for heat observability on almost-Riemannian surfaces
summary: We determine the minimal observation time for the heat equation on a closed almost-Riemannian surface, for a class of observation sets leaving sufficiently thin collars around simple Baouendi-Grushin circles. The structure and density are analytic near these circles, and the coefficients may depend on both variables. The formula is expressed through a complex phase describing concentration near the singular set and extends the thresholds known for separated models. Regular unobserved regions away from the circles do not change this time, provided all other singularities are observed. For singular circles of constant bracket step greater than two, local analyticity implies failure of observability at every time for observation sets at positive distance. We also construct quasimodes concentrated near simple singular circles, with exponentially small errors. Their superpositions give a lower bound for the Schrödinger observation time.

title: KKT Residual Sliding Manifolds: A Projection-Free Structured Finite-Time Solver for Nonlinear Constrained Optimisation
summary: Nonlinear Constrained Optimisation (NCO) requires simultaneous satisfaction of the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions. Existing methods enforce these conditions through projections, penalties, barriers, or sequential approximations, potentially introducing computational complexity and convergence difficulties. For nonconvex problems, a KKT point need not be a local optimum. This paper reformulates NCO as stabilisation of a unified KKT sliding residual manifold and develops SM-KKT, a projection-free solver. Stationarity, equality feasibility, and regularised Fischer-Burmeister complementarity are integrated into a unified residual system, with complementarity encoding inequality feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementary slackness. The manifold's zero set is shown to be equivalent to the KKT conditions. The required Jacobian saddle-point inertia is characterised and shown, under stated assumptions, to be equivalent to the simultaneous satisfaction of the Linear Independence Constraint Qualification (LICQ) and Second-Order Sufficient Condition (SOSC). This characterisation establishes local stability of the structured correction algorithm under these conditions and distinguishes nondegenerate locally optimal KKT solutions from points failing second-order optimality. SM-KKT computes structured primal--dual corrections and applies a discrete sliding reaching law to drive the KKT residual into a prescribed boundary layer in finite time. Four nonlinear benchmarks show recovery of reference constrained optima with KKT residuals below $10^{-6}$, earlier boundary-layer reaching, and favourable KKT accuracy compared with projected primal-dual, augmented-Lagrangian, quadratic-penalty, and log-barrier baselines.

title: Rigidity results for overdetermined problems of p-Laplace equation with spatially dependent data
summary: Let $p>1$ and $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded smooth domain. We study the following overdetermined problem for the p-Laplacian: \begin{equation*} \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} -Δ_p u=f(x)&x\inΩ,\\ u=0&x\in\partialΩ,\\ \frac{\partial u}{\partialν}=g(x)&x\in\partialΩ, \end{array} \right. \end{equation*} where $ν$ is the inward unit normal to $\partialΩ$ and both data may depend on position. A boundary-local version of the moving-plane argument is developed for the possibly degenerate p-Laplace operator. The advantage of this argument is that it avoids the analysis of the degenerate set of the p-Laplacian. Under some reasonable structural conditions, we prove that the solvability of the above mentioned problem forces the domain to be a ball, the source to be radial, and the Neumann datum to be a suitable constant. We also give an explicit formula for the solution. Further consequences include one directional domain symmetry, the conclusion that full rigidity follows from reflection information in any set of directions whose linear reflections generate a dense subgroup of the orthogonal group $O(n)$, and a constant mean curvature characterization.

title: Walk-on-Ambient-Patch: Solver-Adapted Isometric Embeddings for Projected Walk on Spheres
summary: Projected Walk on Spheres (PWoS) solves surface PDEs through ambient sampling and closest-point projection, but tightly folded embeddings can force short steps or ambiguous projections despite simple intrinsic geometry. We introduce Walk-on-Ambient-Patch (WoAP), which treats the embedding as a solver variable. Edge-isometry constraints and tangent-point repulsion separate intrinsically distant regions, optionally in higher codimension; patch states track residual projection branches without introducing PDE boundaries. We analyze the resulting geometry--sampling tradeoff: additional dimensions provide separation freedom but reduce uniform tangent progress, while strong tangent-biased proposals incur large importance-weight moments. Folded-surface experiments demonstrate reduced projection conflicts, a separate hard-constraint pilot verifies metric preservation, and an internal fixed-RMSE comparison favors higher dimensions at stricter accuracy targets. Together, these results motivate choosing the embedding and projection state jointly with the stochastic solver.

title: Surface-to-Volume Homogenization of NonLinear Steklov Eigencouples with NonHomogeneous Orlicz Growth in Perforated Domains
summary: We study normalized principal Steklov eigencouples on periodically perforated domains when both the bulk energy and the boundary normalization have general, possibly nonhomogeneous, Orlicz growth. The surface term on the hole boundaries carries the critical surface-to-volume scaling. For each fixed mass level, the constrained minima converge along the whole family, while selected minimizers, fluxes and Lagrange multipliers converge along subsequences to the corresponding objects of a homogenized problem. In the limit, the bulk operator is given by a convex cell problem, and the boundary term becomes a volume term weighted by the total surface density of the reference hole. The key tool is a strong approximation of the microscopic traces by cell averages, measured in the scaled surface modular.

title: (Super-)fast convergence rates for Chernoff approximations via centered differences and Richardson extrapolation
summary: We use centered differences to construct Chernoff families and derive even asymptotic expansions for their iterated products. Richardson extrapolation is then used to cancel polynomial part and thereby raise the convergence order. As illustrations, we apply the construction to uniformly parabolic, Schrödinger-type second-order operators and to a third-order dispersive operator, obtaining, at extrapolation depth $m$, the rates $ O(n^{-2m}) $ on the Sobolev scales $H^{2m+δ}$, $H^{4m}$, and $H^{5m}$, respectively, with arbitrary $δ>0$. In the analytic category, quantitative all-order estimates allow the extrapolation depth to grow with the base resolution and yield the super-fast rates $e^{-cn^2}$ for the two second-order models and $e^{-cn} $ for the third-order model. The constructions are explicit in terms of the coefficients of the underlying differential operators and do not use the target semigroup in their definition. This provides a constructive positive answer to the challenge of super-fast Chernoff approximation formulated by Remizov in Problem 30 of arXiv:2410.00416.

title: Well-posedness for the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi-Dirac-Fokker-Planck equation
summary:
This paper is concerned with space inhomogeneous Fermi-Dirac-Fokker-Planck equation posed on a classical kinetic phase space. The nonlinear factor $f(1-f)$ appears both in the transport term and in the collison part of the Fokker-Planck operator, accounting for the exclusion principle of fermions. Solutions are subject to the physical constraint $0\leq f\leq 1$.
  Previous existing results have mainly been obtained under suitable smallness or close-to-equilibrium assumptions. A main difficulty stems from the nonlinear and degenerate parabolic structure of the equation. We prove the existence and uniqueness of global solutions without any smallness or close-to-equilibrium assumptions. To construct solutions, we use a vanishing viscosity approximation by adding a Laplacian in the spatial variable. We derive uniform estimates for the regularized problem and obtain compactness in the space of functions of bounded variation $(BV),$ allowing us to pass to the limit as the spatial viscosity vanishes. Since the limiting equation is degenerate with a nonlinear transport, we formulate an appropriate notion of entropy solutions incorporating the kinetic structure of the equation. We prove uniqueness within this class and show that every vanishing-viscosity limit satisfies the entropy formulation. Our result provides a global well-posedness theory beyond the perturbative regime.

title: A ghost-cell immersed boundary method for the shallow water equations on Cartesian grids: mass conservation and wetting and drying over variable topography
summary: A ghost-cell immersed boundary method is proposed for the two-dimensional shallow water equations with a variable bed (topography), solved with an explicit Godunov-type finite volume scheme (unsplit second-order MUSCL, HLLC flux, hydrostatic reconstruction) on Cartesian grids. Ghost-cell methods leak mass through the wall. To find a robust and conservative treatment, eight constructions of the ghost values and a cut-cell form of the continuity equation were applied to seven test problems, which include wetting and drying on sloping beds and a laboratory dam break. In the resulting scheme, the ghost values are interpolated bilinearly at the image point; solid and dry nodes are excluded, and the weights of the remaining nodes are renormalized. Mass is conserved by solving the continuity equation in cut-cell form, while the momentum equations are left unchanged. The proposed scheme is about as accurate as the ghost-cell method without this modification and preserves a lake at rest whose shoreline crosses an immersed wall. Because only the continuity equation is modified, it avoids the treatment of the momentum equations on cut cells (wall pressure, cell merging) that a full cut-cell method requires.

title: Sharp Thresholds for Linear Determinacy and Zero Wave Speed in Lotka-Volterra Competition-Diffusion Systems
summary: We study two sharp competition thresholds in the Lotka-Volterra competition-diffusion system: the zero-speed threshold for bistable traveling fronts and the linear-determinacy threshold for monostable traveling fronts. Building on our previous results on propagation direction and the classification of traveling waves, we derive explicit Gaussian integral representations of both critical parameters, without involving unknown traveling-wave profiles or speeds. These formulas provide exact characterizations of the optimal competition parameters separating the corresponding propagation regimes. The derivation of these representations was assisted by ChatGPT (OpenAI) Pro, while the underlying theoretical foundations were established in our earlier works.

title: $H_2$-optimal model order reduction using hyperbolic geometry
summary: We revisit the problem of approximating a linear time-invariant LTI model by a reduced-order model (ROM) in an $H_2$-optimal sense. A widely used method for computing such ROMs is the iterative rational Krylov algorithm (IRKA). However, in practice, the stability of the resulting ROM is not generally guaranteed. In this work, we develop a novel framework that can be used to obtain $H_2$-optimal models of single-input single-output LTI systems while enforcing stability of the ROM. We use Malmquist-Takenaka orthogonal expansions in the corresponding $H_2$-spaces and their connection to hyperbolic geometry to develop an equilibrium function. We show that the poles of an $H_2$-optimal ROM transfer function are defined by the zeros of this equilibrium function. The resulting nonlinear root-finding problem is solved using a Newton-type method formulated on the products of Poincaré disk manifolds, where updates are performed along hyperbolic geodesics ensuring that the stability constraint is satisfied at every iteration. We present numerical experiments on benchmark systems for both discrete- and continuous-time LTI MOR problems, including examples where IRKA produces unstable reduced models while the proposed method preserves stability throughout the iteration.

title: Regularity theory for lattice based harmonic maps and low temperature Gibbs measures of the spin-$O(N)$ model
summary:
The purpose of this note is twofold. First, we revisit the classical regularity theory of harmonic maps in the setting of maps defined on a lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ instead of $\mathbb{R}^d$ or some other manifold. The target space of our harmonic maps will be spheres $\mathbb{S}^{N-1}, N\geq 2$. A harmonic map $σ: \mathbb{Z}^d \to \mathbb{S}^{N-1}$ is a map which in any finite subgraph $Λ$ minimizes the internal Dirichlet energy $\frac 1 2 \sum_{i \sim j \in Λ} \|σ_i -σ_j\|^2$ given the boundary condition $σ_{|\partial Λ}$.
  One key difference between our setting and the continuum is that our main Hölder regularity statement in a large domain $Λ\subset \mathbb{Z}^{d=2}$ does not require any regularity assumption on the map $σ$ restricted to the boundary of the domain. For example, when $d=2$ and $N=3$, the Hölder regularity induced in the bulk of the domain holds uniformly in all boundary configurations $σ\in (\mathbb{S}^{2})^{\partial Λ}$ (this is in contrast with the continuum which requires extensions in suitable Sobolev spaces).
  The fact we obtain results uniformly in the boundary conditions allows us to extend our results for positive temperatures. Namely, as $T \searrow 0$, we obtain a local regularity theory for all infinite volume Spin $O(N)$ Gibbs measures, at least when $d=2$ and $N\geq 3$.
  We also discuss implications of our analysis in dimensions $d\geq 3$.

title: Preconditioned Latent Variable Proximal Point Method for Optimal Control Problems with Control Constraints
summary: The latent variable proximal point (LVPP) method solves optimization problems in function spaces with pointwise constraints by a sequence of smooth subproblems whose iterates are strictly feasible. We apply it to linear-quadratic elliptic optimal control problems. Control and observation are distributed but may be restricted to subdomains. We prove that the LVPP subproblems are well posed in appropriate function spaces, that the iteration converges for every sequence of proximity parameters with divergent sum, and that it delivers the Lagrange multiplier of the constraint as a by-product. We interpret the Newton step for the LVPP subproblem as a linear-quadratic optimal control problem with a spatially varying control cost, and we show that Newton's method converges locally quadratically. The Newton systems are solved by the minimal residual method with a block-diagonal preconditioner. We prove that the spectrum of the Newton operator with respect to the inner product defined by the preconditioner is bounded independently of the proximity parameter, the iterate, the mesh and the observation and control domains. The results are combined into a complete algorithm, and tested in numerical experiments.

title: Gauge Transforms and Strichartz Estimates for Benjamin--Ono-Type Dirac Equations
summary: For $T>0$, we consider the Benjamin--Ono-type Dirac equation $$ i\partial_tψ(x,t) + D(-Δ)^{\frac{1}{2}}ψ(x,t) = D\,G(ψ(x,t)), \qquad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,T], $$ where $(-Δ)^{\frac{1}{2}}$ is the fractional Riesz operator, $D$ is the Dirac operator associated with the Clifford algebra of signature $(0,n)$, and $G(\cdot)$ a scalar-valued quadratic nonlinearity. Under a pointwise anti-commutation condition on $ψ$ and a uniform dyadic regularity assumption on its spatial Fourier profile, we construct a unit-modulus gauge map $u$ by $ u=\exp\bigl(-iw\bigr),$ where $w$ is a solution of $Dw=ψ$. Assuming, in addition, the stated regularity and commutation conditions on $w$, we show that the Plemelj components $u_{\pm}=P_{\pm}u$ solve a coupled Schrödinger system with gauge nonlinearities $P_{\pm}N(ψ,u)$, where $$ N(ψ(x,t),u(x,t)) = -2P_{-}\!\left[ G(ψ(x,t)) \right]u(x,t). $$ We also obtain a priori estimates for the homogeneous Sobolev seminorms $\dot H^σ$ of $ψ(\cdot,t)$, with at most exponential growth on $[0,T]$, together with estimates for $P_{\pm}N(ψ(\cdot,t),u(\cdot,t))$. Combining these bounds with the homogeneous and inhomogeneous Strichartz estimates for the Schrödinger system, we obtain, for $n\geq 3$ and every sharp Schrödinger admissible pair $(q,p)$, an a priori Strichartz-type estimate for $ψ$ in $L_T^q\dot W_x^{σ,p}$, expressed in terms of the initial datum $ψ(\cdot,0)$ and the a priori controls of $ψ$ in $L_T^\infty H_x^{σ+1}$ and $L_T^\infty L_x^\infty$.

title: A cell problem for the boundary density and approximation of boundary correctors in homogenization theory
summary: We study the boundary corrector $θ_ε$ in the two-scale expansion for periodic elliptic problems with Dirichlet conditions. By results of Gérard-Varet--Masmoudi and Prange, on smooth uniformly convex domains $θ_ε$ converges to the solution $θ^*$ of a homogenized problem with boundary data given by the boundary layer tail $d(n)$, which is determined by a half-space problem for each normal $n$. In the lifted form of Gérard-Varet and Masmoudi, $d(n)$ is given explicitly by the cell correctors and the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator $N_n$ of this half-space problem. Our main result is that $N_n$ satisfies a nonlinear equation on the period cell alone, so that $d(n)$ and the boundary density that represents it can be computed on the cell. This equation is a Riccati equation in which the derivative in depth is replaced by a commutator with the derivative along $n$. This cell problem can therefore be solved by a Riccati doubling algorithm, and we can compute $d(n)$ at irrational normals without rational approximation. Dropping the commutator term in the cell equation gives an operator square root approximation for $N_n$ that captures the leading term of $d(n)$ for small contrast, for the truncated problem. Finally, we approximate $θ_ε$ at finite $ε$ by the sum of two solutions of constant coefficient problems, one with oscillatory boundary data and the other $θ^*$, and test it on the disk.

title: Fundamental solution expansions in stochastic homogenization of parabolic systems with time-dependent coefficients
summary: This paper studies fundamental solutions of uniformly parabolic systems with stationary random coefficients depending on space and time. Under ergodicity and local regularity, we establish quenched Gaussian bounds for the kernel and its spatial derivatives, with stationary random prefactors. A spectral gap assumption gives moments of every finite order for these prefactors and hence annealed Gaussian bounds. We also prove quantitative two-scale expansions for the kernel, its spatial gradient, and its mixed spatial derivative. The error estimates hold in every finite probability moment and retain Gaussian decay. Their dimension-dependent growth is described by a corrector weight, with a single additional logarithmic factor in the derivative estimates. The proofs combine large-scale regularity, extended correctors, weighted estimates, and a parabolic weak-norm estimate. The latter supplies the passage from deterministic pairings to local annealed estimates without interchanging expectation and a supremum over test functions. The mixed-derivative estimate builds on the gradient expansion and does not introduce a further logarithmic loss.

title: Failure Modes of Interior-Point SDP Solvers on Moment--SOS Hierarchies
summary: Standard semidefinite programming (SDP) solvers working in double precision can become unreliable on difficult problems, even when their output appears plausible. We study this issue for SDP problems arising from high-order moment-SOS hierarchies. Three polynomial optimization problems are analysed by comparing standard double-precision computations with reference solutions obtained using the extended-precision solver \mbox{Loraine\,64x4}. We observe two distinct patterns of numerical failure. In \emph{false convergence}, the computed bounds form a smooth sequence but approach the limit at the wrong rate. In \emph{stagnation}, the sequence develops a plateau or oscillations and no longer reflects the convergence of the underlying hierarchy. We introduce an empirical effective condition number based on the positive spectral components of the primal and dual solution matrices. It serves as a warning indicator rather than an error bound, and its growth accompanies numerical deterioration in our examples. We also examine the imbalance between primal and dual spectral conditioning and a Cholesky inverse residuum as potential diagnostic indicators. The results show that solver termination messages and apparently regular convergence curves may be insufficient to establish the reliability of high-order moment-SOS bounds.

title: Limit cycles govern wave energy accumulation in space-time-varying materials
summary: We study the amplification and concentration of wave energy in smooth, periodic space-time media through the dynamics of the characteristic curves of the associated wave equation. In an impedance-matched setting, we show that stable limit cycles attract neighbouring characteristics, focusing the wave energy density. The exponential attraction rate is estimated analytically from the system's Lyapunov exponent. We further show that the attraction of characteristics and energy accumulation persist under a range of nonperiodic perturbations. Finally, we present a Floquet-Fourier numerical method for computing stable and unstable limit cycles and their attraction rates. Throughout, we exemplify the results using the example of modulation given by a superposition of travelling waves, revealing saddle--node bifurcations where limit cycles may appear depending on the relative wave speeds. Full-wave simulations confirm that the characteristic mechanism continues to describe energy accumulation beyond the impedance-matched case.

title: Beyond periodicity: Fourier methods for optimal control
summary: Fourier-based spectral methods provide compact global approximations, permit simple differentiation and integration, and achieve spectral convergence for smooth periodic functions. Their use in finite-horizon optimal control problems (OCPs) is nevertheless challenged by the generally nonperiodic state and control trajectories: endpoint mismatch induces artificial discontinuities and can destroy spectral convergence. Leveraging Eckhoff-type endpoint-correction techniques, we develop a Fourier-based spectral framework for OCPs with possibly nonlinear dynamics and constraints. The correction improves convergence without enlarging the set of decision variables, yielding an efficient finite-dimensional numerical method. Furthermore, we formulate selected dynamics and obstacle-avoidance constraints through Sobolev residual bounds, which incorporate information about the residuals over the entire time horizon and improve constraint satisfaction. Numerical experiments on benchmark problems demonstrate competitive computational performance, lower residual errors, and improved solution accuracy.

title: Existence and uniqueness of viscous-dispersive shock profiles for the Navier-Stokes-Fourier-Korteweg system
summary: We establish the existence and uniqueness, up to translation, of monotone viscous-dispersive shock profiles for the one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier-Korteweg (NSFK) system, provided the two constant end states satisfy the Rankine-Hugoniot and Lax entropy conditions and the shock strength is small. Treating the small shock strength as a singular perturbation parameter, we construct the profiles via Fenichel's geometric singular perturbation theory. We further provide pointwise estimates for the profiles, which are used in the nonlinear stability analysis of generic Riemann solutions to the NSFK system in a companion work.

title: Fresnel scattering for open waveguide networks
summary: This paper concerns the Helmholtz scattering problem for open waveguide networks, extending the analysis from [arXiv:2302.04353, arXiv:2310.05816, arXiv:2401.04674] to plane-wave incident data. We first reduce the problem to a Fredholm second-kind integral equation on an infinite interface. This produces an integral representation of the solution to the original scattering problem, which is then used to obtain detailed asymptotic estimates of the solution at infinity. To leading order and away from the waveguides, the scattered field is itself a plane wave. Its amplitude and phase shift exhibit a jump across a critical polar angle depending on the direction of the incident plane-wave. Our estimates also imply that the scattered field is outgoing in a weak sense, allowing us to establish a uniqueness result. We conclude by calculating the waveguide-mode contributions to the scattered field in a perturbative regime.

title: Borderline double phase functionals with powers of the logarithm: regularity in the vectorial case
summary: We study vector-valued local minimizers of the borderline double phase functional whose integrand is $|D\mathbf{w}|^p+a(x)|D\mathbf{w}|^p\log^γ(e+|D\mathbf{w}|)$, where $p>1$, $γ>0$ and the coefficient $a(\cdot)$ is nonnegative and bounded. If the modulus of continuity $ω(\cdot)$ of $a(\cdot)$ satisfies $ω(r)\log^γ(1/r)\to0$ as $r\to0$, then minimizers are locally Hölder continuous for every exponent less than one. If $a(\cdot)$ is Hölder continuous, then the gradients of minimizers are locally Hölder continuous. In the vector-valued setting these results were previously available only for $γ=1$. The proof combines a comparison with frozen functionals, whose regularity theory applies uniformly in the frozen coefficient, with the higher integrability of minimizers.

title: One-way pressure-independent valves with hysteresis and chattering
summary: We propose a model for the one-dimensional isothermal gas flow through a valve in a pipe. The valve aims at keeping the outgoing flow in an assigned interval; moreover, its opening and closing depend on a further parameter. The model is realized by a system of two conservation laws with suitable conditions coupling the ingoing and the outgoing flow. We study the corresponding Riemann problem, where non-classical shocks show up. Although simple, the model allows to study two key oscillatory behaviors of the flow, which are due, respectively, to the chattering of the valve, especially seen in the numerical simulations, and to the stabilizing hysteresis induced by the valve operation. We characterize the states leading to chattering and show how they depend on the parameters of the model. Through several numerical simulations, we study the interplay between the two above phenomena.

title: Transformed Convexity for Lane--Emden Equations and Torsion on Spherical Domains
summary: We study the geometry of positive Dirichlet solutions on smooth, uniformly geodesically convex domains $Ω\subsetneq\mathbb S^n$, $n\ge2$. Set $p_n^*=2n/(2n-3)$. For the Lane--Emden equation $-Δ_g u=u^p$, $1<p\le p_n^*$, we prove that the set of positive solution pairs $(p,u)$ has a connected component containing the near-linear solution curve and projecting onto $(1,p_n^*]$. Every pair on this component satisfies $\nabla_g^2(u^{-(p-1)/3})>0$ in $Ω$. For the torsion equation $-Δ_g u=1$, we establish $\nabla_g^2\sqrt{u}<0$ for its unique Dirichlet solution in all dimensions $n\ge2$, without an additional diameter or circumradius assumption. In both settings, the solutions specified above have a unique nondegenerate maximum and strictly geodesically convex positive superlevel sets. For the non-power reaction $f(s)=s^p/(1+λs^δ)$, with $1<p\le p_n^*$, $λ>0$, and $0<δ\le(p-1)/3$, we also prove the existence of at least one positive solution $u$ for which the transform $\left(\int_u^\infty ds/f(s)\right)^{1/3}$ has positive definite Hessian. The proofs combine a spherical Schur-complement estimate with a priori bounds and continuation.

title: A Projection Anderson Acceleration Algorithm for Non-quasi-monotone Variational Inequalities with Hölder Continuous Terms
summary: This paper proposes a Projection Anderson Acceleration (PAA) algorithm for variational inequality (VI) problems, where the underlying function is expressed as a finite sum of Hölder continuous functions and satisfies the $σ$-star strongly monotone condition that includes the star strong monotonicity with $σ= 1$ as a special case. In the absence of quasi-monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity, we establish the evaluation complexity of the PAA algorithm for finding an approximate solution. Specifically, for the star strongly monotone VI problems, the PAA algorithm needs at most $O (\log (ε^{-1}) ε^{2 (\underlineα - 1)})$ evaluations of the function and projection for finding an $ε$-approximate solution, where $\underlineα \in (0, 1]$ is the smallest exponent of H{ö}lder continuity of the component functions. We illustrate our theoretical results by numerical examples of non-quasi-monotone complementarity problems and non-monotone semilinear elliptic equations with non-Lipschitz terms.

title: A cell problem for the boundary density and approximation of boundary correctors in homogenization theory
summary: We study the boundary corrector $θ_ε$ in the two-scale expansion for periodic elliptic problems with Dirichlet conditions. By results of Gérard-Varet--Masmoudi and Prange, on smooth uniformly convex domains $θ_ε$ converges to the solution $θ^*$ of a homogenized problem with boundary data given by the boundary layer tail $d(n)$, which is determined by a half-space problem for each normal $n$. In the lifted form of Gérard-Varet and Masmoudi, $d(n)$ is given explicitly by the cell correctors and the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator $N_n$ of this half-space problem. Our main result is that $N_n$ satisfies a nonlinear equation on the period cell alone, so that $d(n)$ and the boundary density that represents it can be computed on the cell. Finally, we approximate $θ_ε$ at finite $ε$ by the sum of two solutions of constant coefficient problems, one with oscillatory boundary data and the other $θ^*$, and test it on the disk.

title: Orientation Estimation of Cryo-EM Images for Molecules with Arbitrary Symmetry by Semidefinite Programming
summary:
This paper extends the non-unique games framework introduced in Bandeira et al. (2020) to address symmetric structures. Precisely, we consider the problem \[ \begin{aligned}
  \underset{g_1,\ldots,g_n\in \mathcal{G}}{\operatorname{min}}\,\, \frac{1}{|S|}\sum_{i,j=1}^n \sum_{s\in S} f_{ij}(g_i s g_j^{-1}), \end{aligned} \] where $\mathcal{G}$ is a compact group, $S\subset \mathcal{G}$ is a finite subgroup of symmetry elements, and $f_{ij}:\mathcal{G}\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is a loss function. A notable example is common lines based orientation estimation of cryo-EM images for molecules with point group symmetry $S$, where $\mathcal{G}$ is the rotation group $\operatorname{SO}(3)$. With a semidefinite programming relaxation, we turn the problem into a convex program that is solved with the alternating direction method of multipliers. Unlike existing approaches which are tailored to specific symmetry groups, ours provides a unified computational framework for addressing all point group symmetries. We demonstrate the applicability of the proposed algorithm on the cryo-EM orientation estimation problem on both simulated and experimental datasets. In particular, our algorithm is effective in generating high-quality ab initio models from only a few class averages computed from experimental images.

title: Local Turnpike Stability for Two-Population Second-Order Mean-Field Game Systems
summary: This paper establishes a local turnpike property for a two-population, second-order mean-field game system with a quadratic Hamiltonian, in which the running cost for each population may depend on both population densities. In the case of two populations, imposing a scalar stability condition separately on each species is not sufficient because it neglects cross-interaction effects. The appropriate requirement is instead a matrix-valued coercivity condition on vector perturbations $(μ_1,μ_2)$, which involves the symmetric part of the linearized interaction matrix together with weighted Poincaré inequalities associated with the two stationary measures. Consequently, in the multi-population framework, diffusion still acts independently on each population, but the interactions are controlled by the full coupling matrix. A naive scalar energy functional fails to capture mixed second-variation terms arising from costs that depend on both densities. We prove that matrix coercivity is precisely equivalent to the strict positivity of this second variation, and we provide a spectral characterization in terms of the principal spectral value of the coupled stationary linearized operator. For linear models with cross-interactions, this yields explicit algebraic conditions that separate stable parameter ranges from unstable ones. In the non-potential framework, the skew-symmetric part of the interaction matrix leaves the coercivity threshold unchanged, but it can induce transient oscillatory dynamics. Moreover, the scalar turnpike theory extends in a natural, though nontrivial, manner to multi-population systems, where stability is governed by the positivity of a coupled matrix-valued second variation that encodes both self-interactions and cross-interactions.

title: Sampling with collective variables: Relative error analysis for umbrella sampling under general conditions
summary: We consider the problem of estimating the expectation of a function (observable) with respect to a high-dimensional probability distribution, under the assumption that a low-dimensional collective variable map captures all the directions of slow mixing for the distribution. More precisely, under the assumption that the fibers of the collective variable map satisfy a log-Sobolev inequality, we establish non-asymptotic relative-error guarantees for this problem using the eigenvector method for umbrella sampling (EMUS). Our analysis applies to both log-Lipschitz observables and indicator of convex sets, and gives complexity bounds that are polynomial in regularity parameters and inverse relative accuracy, and exponential in the dimension of the collective variable space. As a relative error guarantee, our bounds apply to rare event estimation. We consider Gaussian biasing windows defined on a low-dimensional collective variable space and analyze a modified sparse matrix version of EMUS. The bounds quantify the effect of the map through mixing of the conditional distribution and fluctuation of the observable along the fibers.

title: Sharp dimension threshold for unique FKPP steady states and BBM recurrence
summary: We consider the existence and uniqueness of positive, bounded stationary solutions of the Fisher-KPP equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions. We establish that stationary solutions are unique, and exist if and only if the generalised principal eigenvalue is strictly positive (supercriticality), in dimension at most $6$. This is sharp: we exhibit examples both of non-uniqueness and of existence at criticality in dimension $7$ or higher, including for the classical reaction $f(u)=u-u^2$. This proves a conjecture of Berestycki and Graham in the affirmative for dimension at most $6$, and in the negative for dimension at least $7$. We thereby show that branching Brownian motion cannot survive globally without surviving locally in dimension $6$ or lower, but can do so in dimension $7$ or higher, mirroring the classical transition of Brownian motion from recurrence to transience from dimension $2$ to $3$. We further show that relaxing the strong-KPP condition results in a more general sharp dimension threshold for the uniqueness/non-existence result. These results are valid without any regularity assumptions on the domain boundary. As a corollary, we show that solutions of the evolution reaction-diffusion equation are always convergent in the long run in dimension at most $6$, whilst we exhibit non-convergent solutions in dimension larger than $6$.

title: Non-branching properties of Regular Lagrangian Flows and well posedness of the continuity equation in the class of nonnegative solutions
summary: In this paper we deal with the theory of Regular Lagrangian Flows, as initiated in [29] and axiomatized in [2]. In the first part of the paper we show in Theorem 4.3 (see also Corollary 4.5) that the decomposition of $\mathcal{L}^{1+d}$-almost all the space time in a family of (essentially) disjoint characteristics, the technique at the basis of the well posedness in [1] (for planar, divergence-free and autonomous vector fields), and in [13] (for vector fields having a suitable regularity in space, including BV vector fields) is not only sufficient for well posedness, but also necessary. This shows that in many cases the typical uniqueness statement of the DiPerna-Lions theory, namely that the path $\mathbb{X}(\cdot,x)$ is (essentially) unique given the initial position $x$, can, as in the classical theory, be strengthened by saying that the paths $\mathbb{X}(\cdot,x)$ (essentially) do not branch. As the simple Example 1.1 shows, when we consider vector fields with singular divergence well posedness results may hold only for solutions that do not change sign. In the second part of the paper we revisit [8,9] obtaining a well posedness result for special vector fields of bounded deformation and nonnegative solutions, under a mild regularity assumption (5.3) with respect to the time variable, weaker than the space-time $SBD$ regularity assumption made in [9] for nearly incompressible vector fields. Finally, we revisit carefully the constructions of Section 9 of [13], to see how they provide existence and uniqueness for (1.2) assuming $BV$ regularity in space, in the class of nonnegative bounded solutions.

title: Local well-posedness for the exponentially modified Benjamin-Ono equation
summary: We prove local well-posedness for the modified Benjamin-Ono equation in $H^s(\mathbb{R})$ for $s>3/2$. This equation arises as a modified counterpart of the Benjamin-Ono equation through a Miura-type transformation, in close analogy with the classical relation between mKdV and KdV equations. One of the main obstacles is the apparent derivative loss in the quadratic part of the equation. To overcome this difficulty, we introduce a Cole-Hopf transform adapted to the structure of the equation. The map removes the quadratic derivative term and converts the equation into a Schrödinger equation with a transport and a commutator terms that can be controlled without derivative loss. Solutions are then constructed by parabolic regularization, while frequency envelopes are used to obtain the continuity of the data-to-solution map. In the degenerate case $γ=0$, the transform completely linearizes the equation and yields local well-posedness for every $s>1/2$, down to the scaling-critical threshold.

title: Multi-peak solutions for a magnetic nonlinear Schrödinger equation with exponential critical growth in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$
summary: In this paper, we study the following magnetic nonlinear Schrödinger equation \[ \left(\frac{\varepsilon}{i}\nabla-A(x)\right)^{2}u+V(x)u=f(|u|^{2})u\,\ \text{in}\,\ \mathbb{R}^{2}, \] where $\varepsilon>0$ is a parameter, $A\in C(\mathbb{R}^{2}, \mathbb{R}^{2})$ is a magnetic potential, $V\in C(\mathbb{R}^{2}, \mathbb{R})$ is a multi-well potential, and $f\in C^1(\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{R})$ exhibits exponential critical growth. By variational methods and a penalization technique, we prove the existence and multiplicity of nontrivial solutions for sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. If, in addition, $A\in C^1(\mathbb{R}^2,\mathbb{R}^2)$, we show that these solutions have multiple peaks and we establish their concentration behavior and exponential decay.

title: Norm-resolvent asymptotics for the Neumann Laplacian on periodic resonant thin structures
summary: We consider the Neumann Laplacian on a three-dimensional periodic network of thin rods with edge thickness of order $h$ and vertex diameter of order $h^{2/3}$. We extend the fixed-graph resonant reduction to obtain a finite-$h$ periodic graph approximation with generalised norm-resolvent error $O(h)$, uniformly in the Floquet quasi-momentum. An exact gauge transformation identifies the phase-corrected graph fibres with the canonical lattice Floquet fibres, giving the same rate for the global operators. Collapsing the contact points while retaining the ambient edge tangents gives an approximation with error $O(h^{2/3})$. The proof uses a Ryzhov boundary triple and a Schur--Feshbach reduction. The estimates yield quantitative approximation of Bloch bands and stability of open gaps on bounded energy intervals. For the simple-cubic lattice, we refine the known resonant dispersion calculation to obtain a complete band-gap decomposition and $O(h)$ control of the persistence of each fixed finite collection of gaps in the thin structure.

title: Fresnel scattering for open waveguide networks
summary: This paper concerns the Helmholtz scattering problem for open waveguide networks, extending the analysis from [arXiv:2302.04353, arXiv:2310.05816, arXiv:2401.04674] to plane-wave incident data. We first reduce the problem to a Fredholm second-kind integral equation on an infinite interface. This produces an integral representation of the solution to the original scattering problem, which is then used to obtain detailed asymptotic estimates of the solution at infinity. To leading order and away from the waveguides, the scattered field is itself a plane wave. Its amplitude and phase shift exhibit a jump across a critical polar angle depending on the direction of the incident plane-wave. Our estimates also imply that the scattered field is outgoing in a weak sense, allowing us to establish a uniqueness result. We conclude by calculating the waveguide-mode contributions to the scattered field in a perturbative regime.

title: Modeling soliton-potential interactions for the 1-D cubic NLS via an invariant-preserving finite-difference method
summary: We consider the 1-D focusing cubic NLS with a smooth, spatially-dependent potential which decays rapidly as $x \rightarrow \pm \infty$. As is well known, under sufficient regularity conditions, solutions of the cubic NLS with such a spatially-dependent potential conserve both mass and energy. Additionally, in the absence of a potential, the 1-D focusing cubic NLS admits boosted soliton solutions. Furthermore, in the presence of a potential, the interaction of the potential with boosted soliton solutions to the free case is of active interest in the literature, particularly with respect to the dependence of this soliton-potential interaction on the velocity of the incident soliton. We adapt a finite-difference scheme to the setting of a smooth, rapidly-decaying spatially-dependent potential and show that this adaptation preserves the appropriate mass and energy invariants. Additionally, we use this algorithm to model soliton-potential interactions at a variety of incident soliton velocities.

title: What remains when integrability fails? Mathematical structure in the K(m,m) compacton equations
summary:
Peter Lax's 1968 discovery that certain nonlinear wave equations possess operator pairs (Lax pairs) opened the theory of completely integrable systems, yielding exact solutions, infinite conservation hierarchies, and perfectly elastic soliton collisions. When a nonlinear dispersive equation is provably non-integrable (admitting no Lax pair and only finitely many conservation laws), what mathematical structure governs its dynamics?
  The K(m,m) compacton equations, u_t + (u^m)_x + (u^m)_{xxx} = 0 for m >= 2, provide a testing ground: they support traveling waves with compact support, yet fail every known integrability test. We prove universal algebraic formulas determining the shape, width, and speed of every K(m,m) compacton. We develop a constraint-deficit mechanism explaining how the five independent conservation laws constrain emergent amplitudes and suppress the fundamental Fourier mode of the collision debris, while higher radiation modes remain unconstrained. The mechanism's conclusions rest on explicit hypotheses supported by numerical evidence. A phase-plane analysis reveals the compacton as a singular limit of smooth solitary waves through simultaneous regularity loss and support compactification. These results delineate intermediate territory between integrable order and generic nonlinear dynamics, organized by scaling universality and by the constraint deficit of a finite conservation structure.

title: Recovery of Rough Sources in the Inverse Monge--Ampère Problem
summary: We prove that every nonnegative source \(f\in L^1(Ω)\) in the Monge--Ampère equation \[ \det D^2u=f\quad\text{in }Ω, \] on a bounded uniformly convex \(C^{1,1}\) domain \(Ω\subset\mathbb R^n\), \(n\geq2\), is uniquely determined by generalized boundary measurements of Alexandrov solutions. The measurement is the extremal boundary slope, which extends the outward normal derivative and may equal \(+\infty\). For each \(ω\in\mathbb S^{n-1}\), it suffices to know these slopes for the cylindrical Dirichlet data \[ \frac{t_k^ω}{2}|P_ωx|^2,\qquad t_k^ω\to\infty, \] along any sequence of amplitudes, where \(P_ω\) projects onto \(ω^\perp\). The boundary value and extremal slope determine the interior subgradient image up to a Lebesgue null set. An exact change-of-variables formula and a large-amplitude limit then recover the Euclidean X-ray transform of \(f\), yielding uniqueness without a positive lower bound on the source. For nonnegative \(L^\infty\) sources, the extremal slopes are bounded and coincide with the interior normal derivatives, giving a Dirichlet-to-interior-Neumann formulation. The argument also extends to \[ \vartheta(\nabla u)\det D^2u=f, \] where the known weight \(\vartheta\) is locally integrable, Borel measurable, and bounded below by a positive constant. Conditional on existence of the corresponding Alexandrov solutions, the same cylindrical boundary-slope data determine every nonnegative \(L^1\) source.

title: Schauder estimate in large scale for compressible planar cavity flows with fast-decaying vorticity
summary: In this paper, we study planar compressible cavity flows fast-decaying vorticity and establish a Schauder estimate in large scale. As an application, we obtain an a priori asymptotic growth rate estimate of the cavity, that $s^{\frac{1}{2}-δ}\lesssim h(s)\lesssim s^{\frac{1}{2}+δ}$. This is by far the most accurate asymptotic estimate for compressible cavity flows and is probably the first paper that takes vorticity into account in the asymptotic analysis.

title: Fractional Calderón problem with $L^{\infty}$-conductivities
summary:
We study the inverse problem for the fractional conductivity equation with uniformly elliptic conductivities $γ\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$. For every $n\geq1$ and $0<s<1$, we prove that the local exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann map on any nonempty open subset of the exterior of a bounded open domain determines $γ$ uniquely almost everywhere in $\mathbb R^n$. No continuity, Sobolev regularity, or prescribed behavior at infinity is required.
  The proof works directly with the conductivity bilinear form and avoids the fractional Liouville reduction. It combines exterior determination at Lebesgue points, equality of weighted solutions, and a unique continuation principle for the fractional Laplacian in the weighted class \[
  L_s=\left\{
  g\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n):
  \int_{\mathbb R^n}
  \frac{|g(x)|}{1+|x|^{n+2s}}\,dx<\infty
  \right\}. \] Specifically, if $g\in L_s$ and both $g$ and $(-Δ)^s g$ vanish in a nonempty open set, with the latter equality understood distributionally, then $g=0$ almost everywhere. This result requires neither local boundedness nor Sobolev regularity of $g$. Its proof uses the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension and boundary unique continuation for the associated degenerate elliptic equation.

title: An $\eps$-regularity criterion at one scale for 3-D Navier-Stokes equations and improved upper bound on the box dimension of the interior singular set
summary: In this paper, we obtain an $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion at one scale for 3D Navier-Stokes equations using a coarse-to-refined estimate argument based on mean-fluctuation decomposition. Making use of this $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion, we improve the upper bound on the box dimension of the interior singular set to $15/13$.

title: Global existence of large strong solutions to the 3D compressible micropolar equations with density-dependent viscosities
summary: In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem for the three-dimensional (3D) compressible micropolar equations with density-dependent viscosities. By classical $L^p$ estimates to elliptic system, defining suitable energy functions, after the elaborate index analysis, we establish the global existence of strong solutions to the system with all viscosities depending density as long as the initial density is large enough. By product, We also prove the existence of global large strong solutions with only large initial shear viscosity $μ_1(ρ)$ and angular viscosity $μ_2(ρ)$, which consists with the research work \cite{ZZ2014} of 3D compressible Navier-Stokes equations with constant viscosities and improve the recent result of \cite{HLZ} in some extent where they requiring both initial shear viscosity and bulk viscosity to be large.

title: Existence of positive solutions to anisotropic elliptic equations in the entire Euclidean space
summary: In this paper, we research an anisotropic elliptic equation in the entire Euclidean space R^{N} . Under the assumption that the nonlinearity of the equation has exponential or critical growth, we prove, by means of the mountain-pass theorem, that the equation admits a nontrivial positive weak solution. Moreover, applying the mountain-pass theorem and Ekeland's variational principle, we show that a perturbation of the equation possesses two distinct positive weak solutions.

title: Global existence of the $s$-Schrödinger maps in $n \geq 5$
summary:
We study the $s$-Schrödinger map equation \[ \begin{cases} \partial_t u = -u \wedge (-Δ)^s u
  \quad \text{on } \mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}\\ u: \mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{S}^2\\ u(x,0) = u_0. \end{cases} \] For $s \in (1/2,1)$ and $n \geq 5$ we prove that for small initial data $u_0$ in the critical Besov space one can obtain a global solution.

title: Vanishing viscosity limit of the stationary Navier-Stokes equations in an expanding annulus
summary: In this paper, we establish vanishing viscosity limit of the 2D stationary Navier-Stokes equations in an expanding annulus with a fixed width. The flow is subjected to a large perturbation of a rotation of rigid body at one boundary and stays at rest at another boundary. Due to this different boundary condition setting, the boundary layer effects are different near the interior and exterior boundaries, which result in different thickness of boundary layer and different leading order boundary layer equations. We will construct an approximate solution to this 2D Navier-Stokes equations by using higher order asymptotic approximation and show the validity of the boundary layer expansion. The leading order of the Euler solution is the Taylor-Couette flow $\left(Ar+B\frac{1}{r}\right)e_θ$ for some suitable constant $A$ and $B$, which is determined by using the principle of the Prandtl-Batchelor theory. The perturbation of the tangential velocity becomes large as the annulus expands, which causes heavy difficulties when we show the convergence of the approximate solution. Variously weighted energy estimates up to third-order derivatives of the error solution are constructed to close the energy of the nonlinear system.

title: Ground states of a logarithmic Schrödinger equation with a power perturbation in $\mathbb{R}^N$: existence, uniqueness and nondegeneracy
summary:
The objective of this paper is to study the existence and uniqueness of positive ground state solutions of the following Schrödinger problem \[
  -Δu=u\log u^2+μ\abs{u}^{p-1}u\qquad\text{in }\mathbb {R}^N, \] where $N\ge2$, $1<p<2^*-1$ and $μ>0.$ We prove that there exists a positive ground state solution for every $μ>0$ and every such solution is smooth, radially symmetric with respect to some point, strictly decreasing in the radial variable. Moreover, as $μ\downarrow0,$ the positive ground state solutions centered at the origin will converge, uniformly over the ground-state set, to $U_0(x)=\exp(\frac{(N-\abs{x}^2)}{2})$ in the logarithmic Orlicz--Sobolev space and in $C^{2,α}(\R^N)$ for every $α\in(0,1),$ respectively. Furthermore, for sufficiently small $μ,$ we also prove that the positive ground state solutions are unique up to translations and the kernel space of the real scalar linearized operator can be spanned by the translation derivatives. The proof combines minimization on the Nehari manifold with uniform compactness and an exterior coefficient estimate that prevents normalized difference and kernel sequences from vanishing locally.

title: Cubic Nonlinear Schrödinger Systems and Orthonormal Fermionic Ground States in $\mathbb R$
comment: This is an improved version of the manuscripts arXiv:2606.16544 and arXiv:2604.17363
summary: We study the one-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger system \[ -u_i''-2\Big(\sum_{k=1}^N u_k^2\Big)^{p-1}u_i=μ_i u_i \quad \mbox{in } \ \mathbb R,\ \ i=1,2,\cdots,N, \tag{S} \] where $u=(u_1,\cdots,u_N)\in H^1(\mathbb{R})^N$, $μ_1\leqμ_2\leq\cdots\leqμ_N<0$, $1<p<3$ and $N\geq 2$ are arbitrary. For the cubic case where $p=2$ and $N\ge 2$, we establish the following structural results of the system $(S)$: (i) all nontrivial solutions can be classified completely; (ii) the linearized operator at any nontrivial solution is non-degenerate; (iii) exact $L^2$-mass formulas of all nontrivial solutions are derived in terms of distinct Lagrange multipliers $μ_i$. As the applications of the above structural results, we first show that the system $(S)$ with $p=2$ does not have any orthonormal solution for any $N\ge2$. We then investigate a fermionic variational problem $J_N(p)$ with $N\ge2$, whose minimizers correspond to ground states of the system $(S)$ under orthonormal constraints. More precisely, we prove that there exists a sufficiently small $δ_N>0$ such that $J_N(p)$ is attained for any $p\in(2-δ_N,2)$, whereas $J_N(p)$ is not attained for any $p\in[2,2+δ_N)$. These settle some conjectures of [Gontier--Lewin--Nazar, ARMA, 2021] and [Frank--Gontier--Lewin, CMP, 2021].

title: Existence of solution for Schrödinger-Newton system with vanishing magnetic potential
Local Hadamard well-posedness of the 2D primitive equations without thermal diffusion under strict stratification
summary: We study the two-dimensional non-rotating primitive equations with anisotropic viscosity and no thermal diffusion. For doubly periodic perturbations of a hydrostatic equilibrium with an affine temperature profile, we establish local Hadamard well-posedness in Sobolev spaces under strict stratification. The initial horizontal velocity and temperature have sufficient regularity and vanishing vertical means, but need not be small. The estimates close at the same Sobolev order for these variables despite the horizontal derivative loss in the diagnostic vertical velocity. Stratification-weighted energy estimates and a horizontal compensation argument avoid an additional temperature derivative while retaining the full vertical dependence and the vertically homogeneous velocity component determined by periodic compatibility. A one-sided comparison places higher-order norms of the more regular solution only in terms involving lower-order differences.
